## Summary
During the AWS ops sweep for 2026-09-02T17:00:00Z through 2026-09-20T05:05:00Z, the CloudWatch alarm `lmn-staging-private-context-denied` transitioned OK->ALARM twice, at 2026-09-17 20:00:39 PDT and 2026-09-17 21:48:39 PDT.

Alarm configuration/evidence:
- Metric: `AWS/S3 4xxErrors`, dimensions `BucketName=lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071`, `FilterId=all-private-context-requests`
- Threshold: `Sum > 5` over one 300-second evaluation period; `TreatMissingData=notBreaching`
- Alarm actions: none configured
- Metric datapoints in the sweep window: 9 nonzero one-minute datapoints totaling 102 4xx errors; 4 one-minute datapoints breached threshold, max 38. At the alarm's 300-second period, 6 nonzero datapoints totaled 102 errors; 2 breached threshold, max 51.
- Bursts ran from 2026-09-17 18:35 PDT through 2026-09-17 21:59 PDT.

No existing rebar ticket matched `lmn-staging-private-context-denied`, `4xxErrors`, or `private context denied`. CloudWatch log-group inventory still shows only Lambda groups plus `/bedrock/invocation-logs`; there is no obvious S3 access log group in CloudWatch to identify the caller from this sweep alone.

Probable cause: a staging client, test, or integration attempted private-context S3 access without the expected authorization. Confirmation would be an attributed caller/request pattern from S3 access logs, CloudTrail data events, or application-side logs for the 2026-09-17 18:35-21:59 PDT window.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The denied requests for 2026-09-17 18:35-21:59 PDT are attributed to a caller, workload, test, or external principal.
- [ ] The ticket records whether the traffic was expected staging/test activity, misconfiguration, abuse/noise, or an application bug.
- [ ] If the traffic is expected, the alarm threshold/filter or runbook is updated so the same expected pattern does not create untriaged alarm transitions.
- [ ] If the traffic is unexpected, the responsible configuration or caller behavior is changed so private-context S3 access no longer produces repeated denied bursts.

## Verification
Confirm by replaying the same CloudWatch/S3 evidence path over a later window: either the known expected pattern is documented and no longer produces unactionable alarm transitions, or the unexpected denied-request source no longer emits repeat bursts above threshold.
